rationale: Two blocking defects. (1) copilot-chat-otlp now emits a hard block (continue:false / permissionDecision:deny) when analytics is disabled, the project is excluded, or the preferences file is corrupt, so a user who opts out of analytics loses Copilot Chat entirely instead of just stopping collection. (2) updateCopilotAnalyticsPreferences accepts files that readCopilotAnalyticsPreferences treats as corrupt (no numeric version) and neither accepts a connectors array, so the CLI can silently rewrite a file the hook fails closed on, and an array-shaped connectors reads as fully enabled. All three lenses ran; the blind lens was seeded with the production-source portion of the diff only (test files were reviewed by the edge-case and acceptance lenses), hence medium confidence. Deferred (pre-existing patterns shared with claude-code-otlp.preferences.ts / copilot-connector-scope.ts, not introduced here): 5 - lost-update race on concurrent CLI writes, transient EBUSY/EPERM read mapped to corrupt, rename-over-open-file on Windows, shared mutable default record, no schema-version upgrade handling. Dismissed as noise or unreachable: 14 - e.g. missing-cwd exclusion bypass (both hook input guards require a non-empty string cwd), isTracked/onUntrackedHook double-evaluation window, connectorId prototype key (ids are constants), Claude no-flag status/message wording, AnalyticsStore internal shape differing from the plan sketch, blind-lens 'no tests' (artifact of the source-only diff).

findings.title: Update path accepts files the read path rejects
findings.problem: readCopilotAnalyticsPreferences requires a numeric `version` and an object `connectors`, but updateCopilotAnalyticsPreferences does not check `version`, and neither function rejects an array `connectors` (typeof [] === 'object'). A file like {"connectors":{}} is corrupt (fail closed) for the hook but is silently rewritten by `disable`/`exclude`; {"version":1,"connectors":[]} is read as fully enabled with nothing excluded.
findings.impact: The CLI can overwrite a file the hook considers corrupt, destroying the user's evidence/intent, and a malformed file with array connectors fails open for a privacy control. Existing tests only cover invalid JSON on the write path.
findings.recommendation: Extract one shared file-shape validator (object, numeric version, connectors is a non-array object) used by both read and update; add tests for version-less, array-connectors and wrong-shape files on read, on `disable`, and on `exclude`/`include`, asserting exit code 1 and unchanged bytes.

findings.title: Analytics opt-out blocks Copilot Chat itself
findings.problem: onUntrackedHook emits buildBlock(...) for gate reasons analytics-disabled, project-excluded and preferences-corrupt. In Copilot Chat a block is {continue:false, stopReason} on SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit and permissionDecision:'deny' on PreToolUse, i.e. it stops the session, the prompt and every tool call. It also runs before the scope check, so it fires even when the connector is disconnected or the project is outside a project-scoped connector.
findings.impact: A user who runs `codemie proxy analytics disable --copilot-chat-otlp` (or excludes a project) cannot use Copilot Chat at all in that scope - the opposite of the feature's intent, which is only to stop collection. Claude's equivalent silently stops forwarding.
findings.recommendation: For analytics-disabled, project-excluded and preferences-corrupt return from onUntrackedHook without emitting anything (nothing is collected, the user keeps working, `codemie proxy analytics status` explains why). Do this before the unchanged scope/identity tail so a disabled-analytics user is not blocked by the identity-missing branch either. Remove analyticsBlockReason; rewrite the plugin tests to assert no output and no forwarding for each of the three reasons on every enforced event, and keep the existing scope-corrupt and identity-missing tests unchanged for the analytics-enabled case.
